key_insight: Decoupling operating-duration and flow-rate decisions enables PPO to generate efficient multiproduct pipeline schedules while retaining nonlinear hydraulic constraints.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports demand-driven pipeline operations with more stable flow rates and shorter scheduling times without relying on hydraulic linearization.
method: Model scheduling as a semi-Markov decision process with flexible action durations.
Use cascaded dual actors to separate discrete duration choices from continuous flow decisions.
Train with PPO to avoid gradient interference between the two action types.
evidence_signal: On a real-world pipeline in China, comparisons with a single-actor baseline and a Gurobi-solved linearized MILP report near-optimal delivery accuracy, improved flow stability, and reduced solution time.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify performance gains or establish generalization to other pipeline networks and demand conditions.
paper_title: Efficient Detailed Scheduling of Multiproduct Pipelines using Action-Decoupled Deep Reinforcement Learning
